title: Implement session entry cutoff spread liquidity and minimum hold policies
description:
Implement session and market-quality entry policies. In mike_trade/risk/session_policy.py: regular-hours-only entry gating using the New York exchange calendar (America/New_York); configurable entry cutoff (no new entries after N minutes before close) that respects early-close days by deriving cutoff from the actual session close; and discretionary minimum-hold policy that blocks ordinary strategy (discretionary) SELL exits until a configured minimum hold elapses from the first confirmed entry fill, while explicitly NOT applying to protective stops, trailing stops, risk/safety exits, daily-loss exits, manual close/close-all/flatten, reconciliation-driven actions, or optional end-of-day close. Optional end-of-day close remains disabled by default and is not implemented as an entry block. In mike_trade/risk/market_filters.py: spread filter (max spread in absolute Decimal and/or basis points from latest bid/ask), liquidity filter (minimum recent volume/quote size), and fail-closed handling when quote data is stale, missing, crossed/locked, or has unknown provenance; IEX feed provenance must be passed through in the decision for audit. Each policy returns a decision with explicit reason codes and is a pure evaluator taking clock/time and market snapshot inputs (no data fetching, no broker calls). All prices Decimal; times timezone-aware UTC. Write tests in tests/unit/test_session_policy.py covering both modules.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/risk/entry_eligibility.py (from l.3 if present in the same wave branch; otherwise conventions from l.1/l.2) for reason-code and decision conventions
- mike_trade/portfolio/sizing.py and mike_trade/portfolio/budgets.py (from l.2/l.1) for Decimal conventions
- Existing exchange calendar/clock ports, early-close handling, and market data snapshot/quote types with feed provenance and staleness metadata from earlier phases
- Existing configuration models for entry cutoff, spread, liquidity, minimum hold, end-of-day close

Decision budget: do not edit calendar, market-data, or config modules; accept their types as inputs or define minimal Protocols in the allowed files.
acceptance_criteria: A test proves entries are blocked before regular-session open and after regular-session close in America/New_York, including across a DST transition date
A test proves the entry cutoff is computed from the actual session close, so on an early-close day (13:00 ET) the cutoff moves earlier accordingly
A test proves a spread wider than the configured absolute or basis-point maximum blocks entry with a distinct reason code
A test proves insufficient liquidity blocks entry with a distinct reason code
A test proves stale, missing, crossed, or locked quotes fail closed and block entry
A test proves the market filter decision carries the feed provenance (e.g. IEX) through for audit
A test proves minimum hold blocks an ordinary strategy SELL before the hold elapses and permits it afterwards
A test proves minimum hold does not block protective stop, trailing stop, risk/safety exit, manual close/flatten, or reconciliation exits
A test proves end-of-day close is disabled by default
Neither module performs network, broker, or database I/O
tests/unit/test_session_policy.py passes when run on its own with pytest
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
apply minimum hold to protective, trailing, risk, manual, or reconciliation exits
fetch market data or call brokers from policy modules
run broad test suites or backtests
